clue.text: No drugs sign — one seen in park?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stay away from grass, slang for cannabis
second meaning: the notice telling visitors not to walk on the lawn

explanation.walkthrough: Grass is slang for cannabis, so the familiar park notice doubles as an anti-drugs slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the wording of a lawn notice in public gardens and, taking grass as slang for cannabis, a call to abstain.

clue.text: Man sleeping with football team's strikers!

parts.note: a king is a chessman, abbreviated K
the Hammers is the nickname of West Ham United; 'with' just adds it on

explanation.surface: A man asleep in bed with a whole football side's forwards: a tabloid scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Strikers looks like footballers; it is the definition. Knapping hammers are tools for chipping flint. West Ham United is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Knapping hammers are tools used to strike and shape flint, so they are literally things that strike.

clue.text: Muse returning from Dakota region

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so read these letters right to left
the letters are taken out of the words that follow, sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A source of inspiration coming back from the American prairies.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Green colour of a lovebird flying around

indicators.note: a bird flying around moves every which way, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing the green plumage of a lovebird circling overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is the dull greenish-brown shade used for military uniforms and kit.

clue.text: Quickly leave church with plunder

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A thief running out of a church with the stolen silver.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to rob or swindle them, so it is a verb for plundering.

clue.text: Perplexing lout with tacky jewellery

parts.note: a hob is a dialect word for a rustic or lout

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a yob dripping in cheap gold chains.
explanation.walkthrough: This uses an old sense: as well as to hamper, hobble once meant to perplex or put in a difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries such as Chambers record hobble as a verb meaning to puzzle or embarrass, so its present participle matches.

clue.text: Reportedly gloss over corporation

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: to gild is to cover with a thin, attractive coating

explanation.surface: A press report that a company has whitewashed its failings.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is a medieval association of craftsmen or merchants, an incorporated body of members.

clue.text: With skill I stop the growth of vegetable

parts.note: weeds choke plants by stifling them

explanation.surface: A gardener boasting of skill at stunting a vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like plant whose flower head is eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Lethal advice to tourists in Italy?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a warning that visiting somewhere will kill you
setter's reading: the old saying urging travellers to visit a southern Italian city, after which nothing else compares

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb means a city is so beautiful you can die content once you have seen it; read literally it sounds like a death threat.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying recommends a visit to the Bay of Naples as a crowning experience, yet its last word mentions dying.

clue.text: Greed — a sin besetting returning soldiers

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so the sin wraps round the soldiers
returning soldiers come back, so the letters for them are read backwards

explanation.surface: Greed as a vice that tempts troops coming home with loot.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is the usual crossword source for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, a straightforward synonym, and one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Port exporting old English hair

indicators.note: a port exporting something sends it out, so that item leaves the word

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A harbour shipping out old English hair, as if wigs were cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'old' is exported; 'English' is then added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bristle is a short stiff hair, as on a pig or a brush.

clue.text: Ascertained state of a French region

explanation.surface: A finding about the condition of a part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition; it is an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Provençal is the adjective for Provence, the region of south-east France.

clue.text: Mr Donnelly maybe about to see record producer

parts.note: Declan Donnelly is Dec of the TV presenting duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A TV presenter about to meet someone who makes records.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV presenting pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Decca is a long-established British record label, a company that produces and releases recordings.

clue.text: In time computer memory is flipping dead

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the whole is read backwards
one thing placed in another, so the memory goes inside the period

explanation.surface: A computer's memory slowly failing over time until it goes dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no more has ceased to exist, a euphemism for being dead.

clue.text: Special note on half-hearted crowd

indicators.note: with half its heart gone, the word loses one of its two central letters

explanation.surface: A special memo about an unenthusiastic crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of the crowd word is its double letter; losing half of it drops one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something memorable is worth remembering, hence noteworthy or out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Frosty member of parliament?

parts.note: covered in frost and snow, white and wintry
a parliament is the collective noun for a gathering of these birds

explanation.surface: A cold, aloof politician sitting in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: A gathering of owls is called a parliament, so any owl is a member of one; the whole clue also describes the white Arctic species.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowy owl is a large white Arctic bird, wintry in colour and habitat, and owls collectively form a parliament.

clue.text: Work on a big new camper van

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or reshape it, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to get busy on a large new motorhome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are part of the fodder; 'Work' does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnebago is an American brand of motorhome, and the name is used generally for a large camper.

clue.text: Very comfortable with healthy excitement

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: Feeling content, fit and pleasantly thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable can mean financially secure, and well-to-do means prosperous or wealthy.

clue.text: Sacred syllable in Jewish language conjures up moonshine?

indicators.note: placed in, so the syllable sits inside the language's name

parts.note: the language of the Jewish scriptures
the mantra chanted in Hinduism and Buddhism

explanation.surface: A holy chant in Hebrew magically summons drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that moonshine, illicit liquor, is one example of home-made drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is illicitly distilled spirit made at home, an instance of home-produced alcohol.

clue.text: French city risks deposing duke

indicators.note: to depose a ruler is to remove him, so the noble's letter is taken out

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A city in France takes a gamble by overthrowing its duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Angers is a city on the Maine river in western France, the historic capital of Anjou.

clue.text: Hard working American leaves film company

indicators.note: the American walks out, so those letters are removed

explanation.surface: A diligent American quits a movie business.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood film producers such as Paramount are called studios, so the word names a movie company.

clue.text: Transform middle of the road pub

parts.note: MOR is the abbreviation for middle-of-the-road, bland easy-listening music
PH, public house, as on maps

explanation.surface: Turning an ordinary roadside pub into something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of the road' tempts one to take a central letter; it is the music-radio abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To morph is to change smoothly from one shape into another, a synonym for change form.

clue.text: Women's collective invested in share market

indicators.note: money invested in shares is put inside them, so the answer sits within the words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A women's cooperative putting its money into the stock exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the group of wives and concubines of one man, so a collective of women.

clue.text: Young animals born in container

parts.note: a brood of puppies or kittens
B is the abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: Puppies or kittens delivered in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts something inside; here it is just its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter bin is a receptacle for rubbish in a public place, so a container.

clue.text: Dash of turmeric contained in Indonesian island dish

indicators.note: held inside, so the letter goes within the island's name
a dash is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the spice is used

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a pinch of turmeric goes into an island curry.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spiced curry cooked and served in a wok-like pan, a dish from British curry houses.

clue.text: Therefore involves qualification in ban

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap in or include, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: Master of Business Administration, a degree

explanation.surface: A logician's line about qualifying a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade with a country.

clue.text: Telephoned confused laddie about start of lessons

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged word goes round the letter
a confused boy is mixed up, so the letters are mixed up too
the start is the first letter only

explanation.surface: A puzzled Scottish boy rang up about when his classes start.
explanation.walkthrough: Laddie is Scots for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dial a number is to make a phone call, so dialled is the past tense of telephoned's verb.

clue.text: Second eleven maybe has reason boarding crazy form of transport

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a cricket or football side has eleven players

explanation.surface: A reserve side has its reasons for boarding a mad means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' reads as a reserve team, but splits into two pieces. 'Boarding' puts reason after crazy, as a passenger joins a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam locomotive is a railway engine powered by steam, which pulled passenger trains, so a way to travel.
